rubric.role_summary: Principal-level, hands-on pharmacology scientist leading quantitative molecular biology assays and studies of RNA therapeutic candidates, from study design through interpretation of pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, biodistribution, target-engagement, and activity data.
rubric.search_query:
Find candidates for this role:
Principal-level, hands-on pharmacology scientist leading quantitative molecular biology assays and studies of RNA therapeutic candidates, from study design through interpretation of pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, biodistribution, target-engagement, and activity data.
Mandatory professional qualifications:
- PhD in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Genetics, Pharmacology, Bioengineering, or a related field, OR an equivalent combination of advanced training and relevant industry experience.
- Hands-on experience with quantitative PCR methods and molecular assay development.
- Experience designing pharmacology studies and interpreting PK/PD readouts.
- Experience with RNA therapeutic development.
Preferred, not mandatory:
- Deep hands-on experience with quantitative PCR methods and molecular assay development, including work with complex tissue or biofluid samples.
- Ability to design pharmacology studies, interpret pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic readouts, and integrate molecular results with cross-functional datasets.
- Experience with RNA therapeutic development, including preclinical pharmacology data preparation and presentation for scientific and regulatory interactions.
Work location and geographic eligibility:
Accept any one of these geographic alternatives (OR): San Francisco Bay Area, California. Specific cities and metropolitan areas also include any location within about 100 miles (160 km) of them; states, countries, and regions require a location inside them. Onsite work is based in one of these areas.
